page: Amazon Web Services r5.xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 4 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz. Compute features include 35 MB of shared L3 cache and support for instruction extensions such as AVX-512 and AES. System memory consists of 32 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing an elevated 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. The instance comes with no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage, and includes a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and no GPU hardware.

Benchmark results reflect an architecture targeted primarily at memory density over raw compute throughput. In computational evaluations, the instance scored 1026.0 in Geekbench single-core and 2260.0 in multi-core testing, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 3998.02, placing its processing performance in lower benchmark percentiles. However, its memory subsystem registered an average PassMark memory score of 2086.0, accompanied by uncached memory read and write bandwidths of 25.93 GB/sec and 22.49 GB/sec, respectively. Redis SET throughput achieved 3.44 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 3.88 GB/sec.

Given its generous memory allocation alongside moderate compute and network resources, r5.xlarge delivers cost-efficient resource provisioning for memory-bound tasks that do not demand extensive CPU scaling. The absence of local NVMe storage requires architectural reliance on external network volumes for persistence. The instance is suited for in-memory caching layers such as Redis or Memcached, small to mid-sized relational database engines, and lightweight data processing pipelines where dataset footprint exceeds CPU requirements.
